issue: The lesson never teaches going-concern evaluation or disclosure (ASC 205-40), yet four practice items in this module test it: the look-forward period (nd-12) and the disclosures required when management's plans alleviate substantial doubt (nd-13, nd-17, nd-24). No other lesson fills the gap: the only mention platform-wide is one sentence in the optional far-conceptual-framework lesson, and it gives the one-year period only. Nothing anywhere teaches the alleviated vs. not-alleviated disclosures, when management's plans may be considered, or the 'substantial doubt exists' statement.
evidence: grep -rl 'going concern|205-40' content/far/modules/*/lesson.md returns only far-conceptual-framework/lesson.md (line 167: one-year period only), and far.yaml marks that module optional: true. The lesson for this module has no going-concern heading, takeaway, or check. Items nd-12, 13, 17 and 24 are 4 of the 28 practice items (14%).
source: ASC 205-40-50-1 (one year after the date the statements are issued or available to be issued); 205-40-50-6 and 50-7 (management's plans are considered only if it is probable they will be effectively implemented and will mitigate the conditions); 205-40-50-12 (doubt alleviated: disclose the principal conditions, management's evaluation and the plans); 205-40-50-13 (doubt not alleviated: also state that there is substantial doubt)
fix: Add a 'Going concern (ASC 205-40)' section with: management's evaluation each annual and interim period; the look-forward window; the 'probable' threshold for substantial doubt; when plans count (probable implementation and mitigation); a two-column table of required disclosures, alleviated vs. not alleviated; a key takeaway; and an inline check. Add the ASC 205-40 citation to the frontmatter.

issue: Three practice items test interim financial reporting: the estimated-annual-effective-rate tax method (nd-25), allocation of an annual bonus across quarters (nd-26), and a temporary interim LIFO liquidation charged at replacement cost (nd-27). This module (notes, related parties, risk disclosures) does not teach any of it, and neither does any other FAR lesson. A learner who misses them is routed back to a lesson that cannot help. Whether the 2026 FAR Blueprint tests interim reporting at all (rather than BAR) is also unconfirmed.
evidence: grep -n interim content/far/modules/*/lesson.md finds only incidental mentions: far-inventory-valuation (interim write-down recoveries; gross-profit method for interim estimates), far-sec-segments (ASU 2023-07 interim segment disclosures) and far-income-statement-oci (DISE effective dates). No lesson covers the integral view, the ASC 740-270 effective-rate method, or ASC 270-10-45-6(b). Keys are right: nd-25 = 200,000 x 24% = 48,000 - 22,000 = 26,000; nd-26 = 120,000 / 4 = 30,000; nd-27 = replacement cost. One web search (query on the 2026 FAR blueprint and ASC 270) returned no primary or secondary source naming where interim reporting falls.
source: ASC 270-10-45-6(b), 270-10-45-8 to 45-10; ASC 740-270-30; AICPA 2026 FAR/BAR Blueprints (placement not verified)
fix: Confirm Blueprint placement. If interim reporting is FAR, add a short interim-reporting section to the module that owns it (for example far-income-statement-oci) and move nd-25 to nd-27 there (set moduleId). If it is BAR-only, mark the items optional: true or remove them. Either way, take them out of far-notes-disclosures.

issue: Two items test rules that this lesson does not teach and that sit in later modules. nd-14 tests ASC 440 unconditional purchase obligations, which are taught only in far-debt-other (unit u8) and far-contingencies (unit u12), both after this unit-u2 module. nd-28 tests the ASC 250-10-50-4 disclosure for a change in estimate (the effect on income from continuing operations, net income and per-share amounts). No lesson teaches that disclosure: far-accounting-changes covers disclosure only for changes in principle (line 70) and error corrections (line 98).
evidence: Module order in far.yaml puts far-notes-disclosures (u2) ahead of far-debt-other (u8) and far-contingencies (u12). grep -n 'unconditional purchase' finds far-contingencies/lesson.md:114 and far-debt-other/lesson.md:111 only. In far-accounting-changes/lesson.md the only disclosure lines are 70 (principle) and 98 (error).
fix: Move nd-14 to far-contingencies. Move nd-28 to far-accounting-changes and add the 250-10-50-4 disclosure sentence to that lesson. Alternatively, add a short 'Other required notes' section here (commitments, changes in estimate) before keeping the items in this module.

issue: These are single-fact recall items, yet each is labeled skill 'analysis' with difficulty 3 (nd-20: difficulty 2). Recall is 'remembering', so the skill label is two levels off, and the difficulty is inflated. The mislabel distorts the module's reported skill mix, which counts 13 analysis items among 30 MCQs when only about one MCQ (nd-08) is even arguably analysis.
evidence: nd-22 has the same stem as nd-11 ('Which item belongs in the summary of significant accounting policies?') and the same keyed concept (inventory cost method), yet nd-11 is labeled remembering/1 and nd-22 analysis/3. nd-20 is a yes/no recall of ASC 235-10-50-5. nd-17 and nd-24 restate ASC 205-40-50-12. nd-27 recalls ASC 270-10-45-6(b). nd-28 recalls ASC 250-10-50-4. nd-19 recalls ASC 850-10-50-6. None asks the candidate to examine relationships among data or documents, which is the Blueprint's definition of analysis.
source: AICPA Uniform CPA Examination Blueprints, skill-level definitions (Remembering & Understanding; Application; Analysis)
fix: Relabel all seven skill: remembering. Set difficulty 1 (nd-19 may be 2). Re-run the skill-mix tally: the module's MCQs are recall-heavy, and true analysis is covered only by the TBS (see the practice-design finding).

issue: Skill or difficulty is off by one level on these items. nd-08, nd-18, nd-21, nd-23, nd-25 and nd-26 each apply one rule to a short fact pattern or do one computation, which is application, but are labeled analysis. nd-13 is pure recall of ASC 205-40-50-12 but is labeled application/3, which is also inconsistent with its near-twins nd-17 and nd-24. Difficulty 3 is high for nd-21, nd-23 and nd-26 (nd-26 is 120,000 / 4).
evidence: nd-25: one step, 200,000 x 24% - 22,000 = 26,000. nd-26: 120,000 / 4 = 30,000. nd-23: the stem itself states that a severe impact is reasonably possible in the near term, so the candidate only matches the stated facts to the rule. nd-08 is the module's best item, but it still applies one rule (ASC 275-10-50-20) to facts; there is no multi-source analysis.
fix: Relabel nd-08, nd-18, nd-21, nd-23, nd-25 and nd-26 as application. Relabel nd-13 as remembering. Set difficulty 2 for nd-21, nd-23, nd-26 and nd-13, and keep 3 for nd-08.

issue: nd-11 and nd-22 duplicate each other: identical stems, the same key concept (inventory cost method) and the same distractor types (debt maturities, composition of inventory or PP&E). The same 'policies note says how, not how much' fact is also tested by far-nd-pre1, far-nd-chk1 and far-nd-20. That is five classification items on one fact, all asked the same way.
evidence: cues.md Jaccard similarity nd-11 ~ nd-22 = 1.00. nd-11: key (d) 'The method used to cost inventory'. nd-22: key (b) 'The inventory cost method'.
fix: Replace nd-22 with an application item. For example, give five sentences from a draft Note 1 (including a debt-maturity table and an inventory composition breakdown) and ask which one must move to another note. Or delete nd-22.

issue: nd-13, nd-17 and nd-24 are near-identical: 'substantial doubt is alleviated by management's plans; what must be disclosed?', all keyed to the conditions and plans. Practicing one gives away the other two, and the not-alleviated case is never tested.
evidence: Stems: nd-13 'Conditions raise substantial doubt ... management concludes its plans alleviate the doubt. What must the notes disclose?'; nd-17 'Management concludes that its plans alleviate substantial doubt ... What disclosure is required?'; nd-24 'Substantial doubt ... exists but is alleviated by management's plans. What is required?' Keys: (b), (c) and (d), all 'conditions and plans'.
fix: Keep nd-13. Rewrite nd-17 to the not-alleviated case: the key adds an explicit statement that there is substantial doubt about the entity's ability to continue as a going concern within one year after the statements are issued. Rewrite nd-24 to test when management's plans may be considered: only when it is probable they will be effectively implemented and will mitigate the conditions.

issue: nd-19 has three problems. (1) The stem leaves out the condition that triggers the rule: the control relationship is disclosed only when it could make either entity's operating results or financial position significantly different from what they would be if the entities were autonomous. (2) Distractors (b) 'Nothing, absent transactions' and (d) 'Only if transactions occur' mean the same thing, so a candidate can eliminate both together, and the item becomes a 2-option guess between (a) and the implausible (c). (3) The trap label on (d), 'partial-computation', does not fit a non-numeric option.
evidence: Under ASC 850-10-50-6, (b) and (d) are both wrong for the same reason, and (d)'s explanation repeats (b)'s.
fix: Add to the stem: 'The common control could cause either company's results to differ significantly from those it would report if autonomous.' Replace (d) with a distinct misconception, such as 'Disclosure only in the parent's separate financial statements' (trap wrong-classification). Relabel the trap on (d).

issue: The lesson does not teach that a common-ownership or common-management control relationship must be disclosed even when there are no transactions between the entities (ASC 850-10-50-6). The flowchart even starts at 'Transaction with this party?', which implies that without a transaction nothing is disclosed. nd-19 tests this rule.
evidence: The related-parties section lists the four transaction disclosures and the exclusions only. The mermaid root node is 'Transaction with this party?'.
fix: Add a bullet: 'Control relationship: if the entity and others are under common ownership or management control, and the control could produce results significantly different from those of autonomous entities, disclose the nature of the control relationship even with no transactions.' Add a matching branch to the flowchart.

issue: The lesson's related-party definition and flashcard fc2 list 'management and their immediate families' but leave out the immediate families of principal owners. The ASC 850 glossary includes both. A learner could conclude that a 15% owner's spouse or child is not a related party.
evidence: Lesson: 'principal owners (more than 10% of voting interests), management and their immediate families'. fc2: 'principal owners (>10%), management & immediate family'. The ASC 850-10-20 definition of related parties includes 'members of the immediate families of principal owners of the entity and its management'.
fix: Reword both as 'principal owners (>10%) and management, and members of the immediate families of either'.

issue: The special rule for labor and foreign-operation concentrations is stated imprecisely and incompletely. The lesson says to disclose 'the percentage covered and whether agreements expire within one year'. ASC 275 requires two percentages: the share of the labor force covered by collective bargaining agreements, and the share covered by agreements that will expire within one year. The required disclosure for operations outside the home country (carrying amounts of net assets and the geographic areas where they are located) is omitted. 'Are candidates' is also vague. The far-nd-18 explanation likewise never says what is disclosed.
evidence: Lesson text: 'Special rule: all concentrations of labor subject to collective bargaining agreements, and operations located outside the entity's home country, are candidates; for labor, disclose the percentage covered and whether agreements expire within one year when the vulnerability test is met.'
source: ASC 275-10-50-16 to 50-22 (labor subject to collective bargaining; operations outside the home country)
fix: Replace with: 'For labor under collective bargaining agreements, disclose the percentage of the labor force covered and the percentage covered by agreements expiring within one year. For operations outside the home country, disclose the carrying amounts of net assets and the geographic areas where they are located.'

issue: Explanations across the nd-17 to nd-28 block don't teach. Distractor explanations are circular ('Not the treatment.', 'Not the method.', 'Not the computation.', 'That isn't what the rule says.', 'That is not enough.', 'Not on these facts.'). Item-level explanations restate the key without the rule's authority or the computation.
evidence: nd-25 (c) $24,000: 'Not the computation.' The likely misconception (24% x an assumed $100,000 of Q2-only income) is never named. nd-26: the explanation never shows 120,000 / 4 = 30,000, even though calc is true. nd-27: no ASC 270-10-45-6(b) mechanics (COGS at expected replacement cost; the difference is carried as a current liability). nd-20 (c), (d): 'That isn't what the rule says.' nd-18: never states what is disclosed (the two percentages). None of nd-17 to nd-28 cites an ASC paragraph, while nd-03, 08, 12, 13 and 14 do.
fix: Rewrite each distractor explanation to name the misconception and the rule. For example, nd-25 (c): '$24,000 applies 24% to an assumed $100,000 of Q2-only income; ASC 740-270 requires the cumulative YTD method: 48,000 - 22,000.' Add the computation and the ASC paragraph to each item-level explanation.

issue: Some trap labels don't match the misconception the distractor models.
evidence: nd-25 (b) $48,000 is YTD tax with Q1 not subtracted, but is labeled wrong-classification (it fits wrong-period or partial-computation). nd-25 (d) $22,000 is the Q1 amount, but is labeled reversed (it fits wrong-period). nd-20 (d) 'Only for inventory' is labeled partial-computation, though there is no computation. nd-20 (c) 'Only for public companies' is labeled wrong-classification (it fits wrong-rule). nd-19 (d) is labeled partial-computation for a non-numeric option.
fix: Relabel: nd-25 (b) partial-computation; nd-25 (d) wrong-period; nd-20 (c) wrong-rule; nd-20 (d) overgeneralization; nd-19 (d) per the nd-19 rewrite.

issue: Weak distractors and a qualifier cue. nd-09: the key is the only hedged option ('preferably presented ...'), while every distractor makes an absolute claim. Distractor (c), 'optional if the statements include a statement of cash flows', is implausible. nd-20: (c) 'Only for public companies' and (d) 'Only for inventory' are implausible, which leaves (a) 'Yes, in full' versus (b) 'No'. nd-26: (c) '$120,000 in Q1' models no realistic misconception.
evidence: cues.md flags nd-09 (absolutes only in the distractors; key longest) and nd-20 (key much shortest). On inspection, nd-09 can be answered by spotting the only hedged option.
fix: nd-09 (c): use a plausible misconception, such as 'It must be repeated in unaudited interim statements even when policies are unchanged since year-end' (wrong per ASC 235-10-50-2), and give one distractor a hedge. nd-20: make it a judgment item, or replace (c) and (d) with plausible wrong answers ('Yes, the policies note must restate amounts so it can stand alone'). nd-26 (c): replace with '$40,000 a quarter for Q1-Q3' or 'Accrue only when the bonus becomes legally payable'.

issue: Answer cue: the stem asks which disclosure is 'most complete', and the key is the only option that lists everything: relationship, services, $250,000 and $40,000. It is also the longest option. A candidate can answer without knowing ASC 850.
evidence: cues.md: key longest; absolutes only in distractors b, c, d ('Only ...', 'No disclosure'). All three distractors open with 'Only' or 'No'.
fix: Ask 'Which disclosure meets ASC 850?' and write distractors of similar length that each look complete but have one defect. For example: one omits the $40,000 balance; one adds 'on terms equivalent to arm's length' without substantiation; one discloses the CEO's compensation instead of the fees.

issue: Answer cue in a mock-exam item. The key, 'Compensation arrangements and expense allowances in the ordinary course of business', is about twice as long as any distractor and quotes the ASC 850-10-50-1 exclusion verbatim. The distractors are short, concrete transactions, so the abstract, standards-worded option stands out.
evidence: Key length 82 characters vs. 47-52 for the distractors. cues.md: key much longest.
fix: Make the key a concrete transaction of similar length, e.g., 'The CFO's salary and annual bonus under the company's standard plan'.

issue: The explanation for distractor (d) says 'A loss is recognized only if the contract is onerous.' That is IFRS (IAS 37) language. U.S. GAAP has no general onerous-contract rule. A loss on a firm, noncancelable purchase commitment is recognized when the market price falls below the contract price. Stating it in IFRS terms misleads candidates on a U.S. GAAP exam.
evidence: IFRS has not been tested on the CPA Exam since the 2024 Blueprints (far-standards.md 1c). The platform's own far-contingencies lesson (line 36) states the U.S. GAAP rule: 'a loss is recognized on a firm, non-cancelable purchase commitment when the market price falls below the contract price'.
source: ASC 330-10-35-17 and 35-18 (losses on firm purchase commitments); ASC 440-10-50
fix: Change (d)'s explanation to: 'A loss is recognized only if the market price of the material falls below the contract price on a firm, noncancelable commitment (ASC 330-10-35-17); nothing in the stem indicates that.'

issue: The cash-paid-for-interest formula, 'interest expense - the increase in interest payable, ± premium or discount amortization', leaves the sign to the reader and ignores capitalized interest.
evidence: With a discount, cash paid = expense - discount amortization; with a premium, cash paid = expense + premium amortization. ASC 230 requires interest paid net of amounts capitalized.
fix: Write: 'cash paid for interest = interest expense - increase in interest payable - discount (and issue-cost) amortization + premium amortization; disclosed net of interest capitalized.'

issue: The intpd row assumes there is no discount, issue-cost amortization or capitalized interest, but the exhibit does not say so. The lesson's own formula includes those adjustments, so a careful candidate may hesitate. The 20-minute estimate is also generous for 11 straightforward tie-out rows.
evidence: Answer 58,000 = 64,000 - 6,000. This is correct only if no amortization or capitalization applies. Time estimate: 11 rows at roughly 1 minute each, plus reading the exhibits, is about 10 to 14 minutes.
fix: Add to the exhibit: 'No interest was capitalized, and the debt has no discount or issue costs.' Consider minutes: 15.

issue: The wording of the required related-party disclosures is slightly loose. The lesson and fc3 say 'the effects of any change in terms'; ASC 850 says 'the effects of any change in the method of establishing the terms from that used in the preceding period'. The ASC 850-10-50-1(d) requirement to disclose the terms and manner of settlement of balances (if not otherwise apparent) is omitted.
evidence: Lesson item 3: 'The dollar amounts of transactions and the effects of any change in terms'. fc3: 'Dollar amounts (and changes in terms)'.
fix: Reword item 3 as '... and the effects of any change in the method of establishing the terms', and add to item 4 '(and, if not otherwise apparent, the terms and manner of settlement)'. Mirror the change in fc3.

issue: The lesson has one pre-question (on the policies note) and two inline checks (policies note; supplier concentration). Nothing primes or checks related parties, which are the most-tested topic here (12 of 30 MCQs), or the tie-out skill behind the analysis objective and the TBS.
evidence: preQuestions: [far-nd-pre1]. Check blocks: far-nd-chk1 (policies) and far-nd-chk2 (concentration) only. The related-parties and 'Tying the notes' sections have no check.
fix: Add a pre-question on arm's-length representations or principal owners, an inline check after the related-parties section (e.g., compensation vs. loan to an officer), and a numeric check after 'Tying the notes' (e.g., cash paid for interest).

issue: Practice-set design: no MCQ exercises the module's analysis objective (compare note disclosures with the statements and support). Only the TBS does. The nominally 'hard' end of the set (nd-17 to nd-28, all difficulty 3) is short recall, and only nd-08 is genuinely difficult, so the easy-to-hard progression is nominal. With corrected labels the MCQ mix is about 16 remembering, 13 application and 1 analysis, against the FAR Blueprint's 5-15% remembering, 45-55% application and 35-45% analysis allocation.
evidence: Objective 4 (analysis) has no MCQ. Relabelled skill counts come from the two skill-label findings above; the current labels show remembering 9, application 8 and analysis 13.
fix: Add 3-4 application or analysis MCQs drawn from the tie-out section: cash paid for interest from expense and payable changes; whether a maturity table agrees to the current portion; depreciation vs. D&A; and spotting an unsubstantiated arm's-length claim in a draft note. Order practice items easy to hard.
